meta.title: Travis County — the money trail
meta.note: Texas counties budget fund by fund, not as one grand total. This shows the tax-supported budget — the General Fund, the Road & Bridge Fund, and Debt Service — adopted by the Commissioners Court in September 2025 for the year beginning October 1, 2025. It is paid for mostly by property tax: the adopted rate is $0.375845 per $100 of value (maintenance & operations $0.333824 + debt $0.042021), the voter-approval maximum. Counting every fund (internal-service and grant/capital funds, and net of inter-fund transfers), the county’s all-funds budget is about $2.16 billion; those other funds are left out of the total here because they largely recirculate money already counted. Every figure traces to the county’s adopted budget and its Recapitulation Financial Statement.

nodes.name: General Fund
nodes.note: The county’s main operating fund, paid mostly by property tax. The biggest offices inside it: the Sheriff (patrol + the jail) $252.9M, Transportation & Natural Resources $91.4M, Technology & Operations $83.0M, Health & Human Services $71.8M, Juvenile Probation $54.7M, the District Attorney $36.6M, and EMS $29.0M. The tree below groups spending by function, as the county’s own financial statement does; note the Sheriff’s budget spans both Corrections and Public Safety, so a single “policing” figure would overstate it.

nodes.name: General Government
nodes.note: Countywide administration, elections, records, tax collection, and the commissioners/judge offices.

nodes.name: Justice System
nodes.note: The courts, District and County Attorneys, District and County Clerks, and related legal services.

nodes.name: Corrections & Rehabilitation
nodes.note: The county jail (the Travis County Correctional Complex) and rehabilitation programs. Run by the Sheriff.

nodes.name: Public Safety
nodes.note: Law-enforcement patrol, the constables, and emergency response. (The Sheriff’s office spans this and Corrections.)

nodes.name: Health & Human Services
nodes.note: County health, mental-health, and social services.

nodes.name: Infrastructure & Environmental
nodes.note: Transportation and natural resources, facilities, and environmental work in the unincorporated county.

nodes.name: Community & Economic Development
nodes.note: Community services, veterans, and economic development.

nodes.name: Reserves (unallocated, allocated & general-purpose)
nodes.note: Travis County carries large General-Fund reserves — unallocated ($157.6M), allocated ($58.5M), other general-purpose ($167.0M), and special-purpose ($96.2M). Reserves are budgeted but held, not spent, unless the Commissioners Court appropriates them.

nodes.name: Debt service & interest (within the General Fund)
nodes.note: Interest costs carried inside the General Fund.

nodes.name: Transfers out
nodes.note: Money moved from the General Fund to other funds.

nodes.name: Road & Bridge Fund
nodes.note: County roads and bridges in the unincorporated areas, funded by a share of property tax and road revenues.

nodes.name: Debt Service Fund
nodes.note: This year’s principal and interest on the county’s tax-supported debt (the I&S property-tax rate funds it). Total outstanding debt obligations were about $1.17 billion as of the FY2026 budget.
